item.title: Iceland’s ‘No’ Camp in Narrow Lead Ahead of Saturday’s EU Vote
item.description: Iceland is set for a close result in Saturday’s referendum on resuming accession talks with the European Union, with the latest poll showing opponents slightly ahead of proponents for the first time.
item.dc:creator: Ragnhildur Sigurdardottir

item.title: China Tells Japanese Lawmakers Taiwan Is at Heart of Tensions
item.description: A senior Chinese diplomat told a group of Japanese lawmakers that history and Taiwan are at the center of tensions between the nations, saying Tokyo needed to take “concrete actions” for them to improve.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: UK Delayed Drive to Prepare Brits for Crises Over Vibe Worries
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham pushed back plans for a nationwide campaign telling Britons how to prepare for emergencies over concerns it would risk being seen as an overly pessimistic start to his premiership.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Milligan

item.title: Jakarta Police Survey Damage After Protest Escalates Overnight
item.description: Jakarta police officers are surveying the damage from a protest at parliament that started Thursday and stretched into early Friday morning.
item.dc:creator: Norman Harsono

item.title: US Commander Declares Hormuz Shipping Lanes Are Mine-Free
item.description: The top US commander for the Middle East said that American forces have cleared Iranian mines from the Strait of Hormuz, after Washington’s allies expressed doubts about similar claims by President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: John Harney

item.title: Trump Says Putin Will Not Be Attacking NATO Territory | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/27/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Jessica Taylor, Senate and Governors Editor at the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter, says public and private polling shows the Texas Senate race essentially tied, with Ken Paxton's political and personal baggage helping put the state in play for Democrats. Former US Ambassador to NATO Ivo Daalder says the Trump administration lacks a concerted strategy to pressure Russia into negotiations, arguing Washington needs to combine continued military support for Ukraine with stronger economic pressure and diplomacy. Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller says President Trump's push to bring in more foreign beef is hurting US ranchers and could cost Republicans support in the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Miller: Beef Policy Could Cost GOP in Midterms
item.description: Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller says President Trump's push to bring in more foreign beef is hurting US ranchers and could cost Republicans support in the midterm elections. Miller, a strong Trump supporter, says he had a "heated discussion" with Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins over the policy and calls for mandatory country-of-origin labeling for beef. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lack of Russia Pressure Strategy a 'Problem': Daalder
item.description: Former US Ambassador to NATO Ivo Daalder says the Trump administration lacks a concerted strategy to pressure Russia into negotiations, arguing Washington needs to combine continued military support for Ukraine with stronger economic pressure and diplomacy. He also sees little prospect that Chinese President Xi Jinping's upcoming visit to Washington will produce progress toward ending the war. Daalder speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Taylor: Paxton's Baggage Puts Texas In Play for Dems
item.description: Jessica Taylor, Senate and Governors Editor at the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter, says public and private polling shows the Texas Senate race essentially tied, with Ken Paxton's political and personal baggage helping put the state in play for Democrats. Taylor says trade tensions with Canada could also have political consequences in battleground states including Michigan and Ohio, where tariffs may cut both ways with voters. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Tyler Kendall on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Taps Ben Moss to Be Next White House Staff Secretary
item.description: President Donald Trump said Ben Moss would become his new staff secretary, replacing Will Scharf, who is taking on a new role as the next White House counsel.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan

item.title: Venezuela Weighs OPEC Exit as US Discusses Oil Fields Stake
item.description: Venezuela is considering whether it should quit OPEC, according to people familiar with the matter, potentially delivering a fresh blow to the oil cartel it helped create more than six decades ago.
item.dc:creator: Ben Bartenstein, Mie Dahl and Fabiola Zerpa

item.title: DOJ to Challenge Dismissal of Harvard Civil Rights Suit
item.description: The Trump administration told a federal judge it will challenge the dismissal of its lawsuit against Harvard University alleging that the school violated civil rights laws by failing to protect Jewish and Israeli students after the October 2023 attack by Hamas on Israel.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dolmetsch

item.title: Nvidia Rally, AI Trade & Jackson Hole Preview | The Close 8/27/2026
item.description: Bloomberg Television brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Robinhood Markets CIO Stephanie Guild, Everpure Chairman & CEO Charlie Giancarlo, New Street Research Equity Research Analyst, Technology Infrastructure Antoine Chkaiban, Agilent Technologies CEO Padraig McDonnell, Nuveen CIO Saira Malik, American Century Investment CIO, Multi-Asset Strategies, Senior Vice President Rich Weiss, RBC Capital Markets Managing Director, Software Equity Research Rishi Jaluria, Bain Capital Partner & Head of Real Estate Ryan Cotton, & Morgan & Morgan Founder John Morgan. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ‘Lake Ontario’ Hat Maker Sees Politics and Sales in Trump’s Name Change
item.description: Mere hours before President Donald Trump signed an order to change Lake Ontario’s name on US maps, a husband-and-wife team in Canada’s capital city began marketing a blue hat with its name.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Morgan

item.title: Morgan & Morgan Founder: Firm Is Worth ‘At Least $10 Billion'
item.description: John Morgan has grown his legal practice Morgan & Morgan into a multi-billion dollar empire spanning all 50 states. His book "Life Is Luck: Lessons From a Paperboy and How to Improve Your Luck", details the lessons he's learned in his very full life. Morgan sat down with Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to discuss his company's growth, private equity, and his book "Life Is Luck: Lessons From a Paperboy and How to Improve Your Luck". (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Lutnick Blames Carney, Politics for Collapse of Trade Talks
item.description: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick accused Canada of scuttling trade talks by adding last-minute demands, saying Prime Minister Mark Carney had political incentives to kill an emerging deal.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove

item.title: Nvidia Fuels AI Trade, Warsh Countdown | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/27/2026
item.description: Nvidia's blockbuster earnings report spurred a rally in tech stocks, bolstering confidence once more in the AI trade that has powered the US bull market. Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Ian King joins to recap the numbers. Then, Bloomberg TV and Radio International Economics & Policy Correspondent Michael McKee joins live from Jackson Hole, Wyoming as markets count down to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Friday remarks. Jack Manley, Global Market Strategist, JPMorgan Asset Management weighs in on today's trade and Fed expectations. Plus, Nina Trentmann, Bloomberg News CFO Briefing Editor joins alongside Eric Aboaf, CFO of S&P Global, to discuss the firm's recent earnings results and spin-off of Mobility Global. Finally, Matthew O'Neill, Co-Producer & Co-Director of the documentary film 'Can’t Look Away: The Case Against Social Media,' joins to discuss Meta's $18 billion settlement over claims of youth addiction to social media. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jackson Hole Fed Meeting: Warsh Faces Crucial Wall Street Test
item.description: Investors reacted harshly after the Fed chairman’s press conference last month.
item.dc:creator: Enda Curran

item.title: US in Talks With Venezuela to Take Major Stake in Oil Fields
item.description: The US is in talks with Venezuela to take a large stake in its oil fields, a dramatic move that would extend the Trump administration’s influence on the post-Maduro government and the nation’s vast energy reserves.
item.dc:creator: Fabiola Zerpa and Mie Dahl

item.title: Top House Democrat Probes 1789 Capital on Trump Family Ties
item.description: The top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee launched an investigation into 1789 Capital, a venture capital firm with ties to President Donald Trump’s eldest son, questioning the fund’s investments in companies boosted by the administration.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly and Annie Massa
